slides: Before you practice, here's a quick summary of the topic. What the letters mean, the four steps, and the number facts.

slides.say: A bar on top means the letters are the digits of one number. A B is ten A plus B, not A times B. And A B C is a hundred A, plus ten B, plus C.
The same letter is always the same digit, and a leading digit is never zero. Different letters? Only if the question says so.
Write it vertically, check the units digit, check the leftmost digit and the size, and then plug in. One letter asked? Plug in the choices.

A puzzle in words, with no columns? Write the number as ten A plus B, and collect the letters on each side. Ten A plus B equals three times A plus B gives seven A equals two B, so the number is twenty-seven.
In the ones column nothing carries in, so X plus Y ends in X means Y is zero. In any other column there may be a carry, so it's zero or nine.
Two numbers, and the sum has more digits? The leading digit is one. Seventy-six plus fifty-eight is one thirty-four. Only for two numbers.
The special digits, zero, one, five and six, keep their units digit when multiplied by themselves. Fifteen times fifteen is two twenty-five, and sixteen times sixteen is two fifty-six.
A subtraction? Flip it into an addition. A division? Flip it into a multiplication.
A number plus its reversal divides by eleven, minus its reversal by nine, and with three digits, by ninety-nine.
A A A is a hundred eleven times A, so it divides by three and by thirty-seven. Four forty-four is thirty-seven times twelve.
at: A A A is a hundred eleven
